name: calls.add

external_unique_id.desc: An ID supplied by the 3rd-party Call provider. It must be unique across all Calls from that service.

external_display_id.desc: An optional, human-readable ID supplied by the 3rd-party Call provider. If supplied, this ID will be displayed in the Call object.

join_url.desc: The URL required for a client to join the Call.

desktop_app_join_url.desc: When supplied, available Slack clients will attempt to directly launch the 3rd-party Call with this URL.

date_start.desc: Unix timestamp of the call start time.

created_by.desc: The valid Slack user ID of the user who created this Call. When this method is called with a user token, the created_by field is optional and defaults to the authed user of the token. Otherwise, the field is required.

users.desc: The list of users to register as participants in the Call. Read more on how to specify users here.

safety_note_for_agents: This catalog documents Slack's UNDOCUMENTED/internal API surface for a specific workspace (Hack Club, Enterprise Grid). Calling an undocumented method with params_known=false means you would be guessing params against a real backend with unknown side effects -- do not do this against a real account/token without a human in the loop, and never call anything shaped like a write (*.delete, *.set, *.remove, *.create, *.update, and similar) without explicit human confirmation and a clear understanding of the blast radius, even when params_known=true. 'existence-only' verified does NOT mean 'safe to call' -- it only means the method name is real.
